answer: Every identity is a vertex in the work graph, each working on its own island of tasks. The network records the behavioral echo of each vertex: task timing, choice patterns, response latency. Two vertices whose echoes match above 90 percent are frozen and their 30 POA bonds burned. Faking one distinct echo costs real compute and operator time, so an attacker pays 30 POA plus a unique behavior profile per fake identity. Cost scales linearly per fake, and detection gets stronger as more fakes echo each other.
